title: Desmarets to an unnamed correspondent, Marly, 4 June 1710 (DECODE R10198)

steps.what: Fetched record metadata and three page images from DECODE with the shared cookie; only 590 px exists.
Transcribed 34 French/figure line pairs and 22 figure-only lines from 3x enlarged crops.
French lines are an interlinear decipherment; build key by aligning them to the figures (letter EM per line, global, with boundary priors; word-level EM).
Line-offset overlap test and repeat/frequency statistics: figures are a real code (183 types/471, repeated 6-gram) but not the text above them.
Web search for a printed text; DECODE key records 1700-1715 for a French ministerial key.
Issue #28 (yuanyi-350) reported that Tomokiyo's published 1710 table reads the letter if the 471 groups are concatenated instead of read line by line.

Fetched Cryptiana 11B (louisxiv.htm): the table (built from Pillon's alignment) and the note that the unglossed tail is the decipherment written out of sync (printed in L'Intermediaire des curieux 50, 1904).

Transcribed the table from its image (tomokiyo_decode.py) and decoded the transcription as one stream: 456 of 471 groups (96.8%) in the table, the whole letter including the 22 figure-only lines reads as sense; 12 group types (15 tokens) not in the table, values inferred from context and marked.
Compared the stream with the 34 interlinear French lines and the closing clear formula; the earlier conclusion that the French is not the decipherment was an artefact of per-line alignment.

outcome.method_basis: Tomokiyo's published reconstruction of the 1710 code, derived from this letter, applied to the 471 groups read as one stream.
outcome.fraction_read_source: tomokiyo_decode.py: 456 of 471 code-group tokens have a value in Tomokiyo's table and read as sense; reading.txt

gaps.detail: Not in Tomokiyo's table; 94 (ce), 539 (l'esper) and 565 (oit) are clear from the context, the others are plausible readings only (559 may be a null).

outcome.notes: Earlier attempt (21 Sept 2026) closed as 'not decoded' after four per-line alignment models; Issue #28 corrected it. Tomokiyo's table is itself a reconstruction from this letter, so the reading is checked against the sheet's own decipherment, not independent of it.

prior.where: Tomokiyo's reconstruction table (Cryptiana 11B, with Alexandre Pillon's alignment); clear text printed in L'Intermediaire des curieux 50 (1904); the interlinear French on the sheet itself

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded. Issue #28 (yuanyi-350, 9 Oct 2026) pointed to Tomokiyo's 1710 table and to the continuous-stream reading; this was checked and written up here.
